mainTopic: The sources for the twenty-אמה limit of a סוכה, רב's rulings that narrow the מחלוקת, and the story of הילני המלכה's tall סוכה
overview: Earlier on the דף, רבה, רבי זירא and רבא each gave a different source and reason for why a סוכה taller than twenty אמות is פסול. The גמרא first explains why each one rejects the others' sources: every source has a weak point. Next it brings three reports of a ruling by רב that narrow the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the חכמים. רבי יאשיה's report (walls that reach the סכך) fits רבה's reason. רב הונא's report (a סוכה bigger than four by four אמות) fits רבי זירא's reason. רב חנן בר רבה's report (anything bigger than head, most of body and table) fits none of them. The גמרא shows that רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבה agree on the minimum size of a סוכה and differ only on how far the מחלוקת reaches. Then a ברייתא tells of הילני המלכה's tall סוכה, and the גמרא explains why רבי יהודה needed both of his answers to the חכמים. Finally the גמרא starts testing that story against the reports of רב, and the test continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the others reject רבה's source
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבא do not learn from רבה's פסוק, because to them that פסוק is about passing down the memory of יציאת מצרים to future generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them do not learn it like רבה, because that פסוק is about knowledge for the generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why each אמורא rejects the others' sources. It starts with רבה's source, 'למען ידעו דורותיכם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה read 'so that your generations will know' as meaning a person must know he is sitting in a סוכה. The others read it differently: future generations must know the story of יציאת מצרים. On their reading, the פסוק says nothing about how high a סוכה may be.

keyTerms.meaning: all of them (here: the other אמוראים)
for the generations, for all future times
they do not say, they do not accept

phrases.english: All of them do not say like Rabba,
that is knowledge for the generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלְּהוּ כְּרַבָּה לָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the explanation of why the three sources are mutually rejected, after the three sources were presented earlier on the דף.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבה's use of the פסוק as the source for the twenty-אמה rule, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק means future generations must know about יציאת מצרים. It does not mean the person in the סוכה must be aware of it.

steps.title: Why the others reject רבי זירא's source
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבא do not learn from רבי זירא's פסוק, because it describes the days of משיח and not a physical סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also do not learn it like רבי זירא, because that פסוק is written about the days of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why רבה and רבא reject רבי זירא's source, 'וסוכה תהיה לצל יומם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיה describes a future time when הקב"ה will shelter the Jewish people. רבה and רבא hold that 'סוכה' there is just a picture of that protection. So the פסוק teaches nothing about the הלכות of building a סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: the days of משיח, the future redemption

phrases.english: They also do not say like Rabbi Zeira,
that verse is written about the days of Mashiach.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא נָמֵי לָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern, now applied to the second אמורא's source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using ישעיה's פסוק as a halachic source about סוכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is a prophecy about the days of משיח, so it is not a law about building a סוכה.

steps.title: רבי זירא defends his source
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the נביא could have said 'חופה' (canopy), the word used in the פסוק just before. Using the word 'סוכה' teaches two things: the prophecy, and that a סוכה is meant to give shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי זירא answer? If so, the פסוק should have said 'a canopy shall be for shade by day.' Why does it say 'a סוכה shall be for shade by day'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי זירא would answer the objection from the last step. It then gives his reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא agrees the פסוק is about משיח's time. But the extra choice of the word 'סוכה' instead of 'חופה' shows that the פסוק also teaches about a real סוכה. A סוכה's job is to give shade from its סכך, and above twenty אמות the walls give the shade instead.

keyTerms.meaning: let the פסוק say (it should have said)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא does not deny that the פסוק is about משיח. He agrees, and says the פסוק teaches the halacha about סוכה as well.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira?
phrases.notes: This is short for: how would רבי זירא answer this?

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"And a canopy shall be for shade by day,"
phrases.notes: The word חופה is used in the פסוק right before (ישעיהו 4:5).

phrases.english: so what is "and a sukkah shall be for shade by day"?
Learn from it two things.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא — אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the rejection in step 2 on behalf of רבי זירא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: the unusual word choice shows a second lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק is about משיח, it cannot teach סוכה law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'סוכה' instead of 'חופה' shows that the פסוק teaches both the prophecy and that a סוכה must give shade.

steps.title: Why the others reject רבא's source
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבי זירא do not learn from רבא's פסוק because of אביי's earlier question about a סוכה with iron walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also do not learn it like רבא, because of אביי's difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the pattern by explaining why רבה and רבי זירא reject רבא's source, 'בסוכות תשבו שבעת ימים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a סוכה must be a temporary dwelling, so a very tall, permanent-style building is פסול. אביי had challenged this: if someone built very strong iron walls and put סכך on top, would that be פסול too? That challenge weakens רבא's reasoning, so the others do not rely on it.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three sources has a weak point in the eyes of the others. רבה's פסוק is about memory for future generations, רבי זירא's פסוק is about משיח, and רבא's reasoning has אביי's difficulty. So each אמורא keeps his own source.

phrases.english: They also do not say like Rava,
because of Abaye's difficulty.
phrases.notes: This is אביי's question from earlier: a סוכה made with iron walls is not temporary at all, so would it be פסול?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרָבָא נָמֵי לָא אָמְרִי, מִשּׁוּם קוּשְׁיָא דְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part explanation, now applied to the third אמורא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's source and the temporary-dwelling reasoning behind it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי's case of iron walls shows a problem with the 'temporary dwelling' reasoning.

steps.title: Whose view fits רבי יאשיה's report of רב about walls reaching the roof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב's statement, reported by רבי יאשיה. It says the argument about a very tall סוכה is only when the walls do not reach the סכך, and asks which earlier reason it fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what רבי יאשיה said in the name of רב? רב said the argument is only when the walls do not reach up to the roofing. But if the walls do reach the roofing, the סוכה is kosher even above twenty אמות. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a rule from רב and asks which of the earlier reasons for the twenty-אמה limit it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב limits the argument in the משנה: if the walls go all the way up to the סכך, even the חכמים agree a tall סוכה is kosher. The question is which reason (רבה's, רבי זירא's, or רבא's) would explain why touching walls make a difference.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this
that Rabbi Yoshiya said that Rav said:
The dispute is where the walls do not reach the roofing,
phrases.notes: This is the argument in the משנה between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about a סוכה taller than twenty אמות.

phrases.english: but where the walls reach the roofing,
even above twenty cubits it is kosher.
In accordance with whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing why each אמורא rejected the others' פסוקים, the גמרא applies their reasons to a statement of רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason for the twenty-אמה limit explains why walls reaching the סכך make a tall סוכה kosher?

steps.title: It fits רבה: when the walls reach the roof, the eye notices it
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule follows רבה, who said a tall סוכה is not kosher because the eye does not notice the סכך. Walls going up to the roof lead the eye to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבה, who said the reason is that the eye does not notice the roof. Since the walls reach the roofing, the eye does notice it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's rule matches רבה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the problem with a tall סוכה is that a person does not see the סכך. When the walls go straight up to the סכך, the eye follows them up and sees it, so the problem is gone. That is why רב said even the חכמים would agree.

keyTerms.meaning: The eye catches sight of it
It surely does catch (a doubled verb for emphasis)

phrases.english: Like Rabba, who says
it is because the eye does not catch sight of it,
and since the walls reach the roofing,
the eye does catch sight of it.
phrases.notes: The eye follows the walls all the way up, so it reaches the roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבָּה, דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא שָׁלְטָא בַּהּ עֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's rule follows רבה, since walls reaching the סכך solve the problem of the eye not seeing it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה's report of רב (walls reaching the roof) follows רבה's reason: seeing the סכך.

steps.title: Whose view fits רב הונא's report of רב about a large סוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another statement of רב, reported by רב הונא. It says the argument is only about a סוכה of four by four אמות, and asks whose reason it fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what רב הונא said in the name of רב? רב said the argument is only when the סוכה is just four by four אמות. But if it is larger than four by four אמות, it is kosher even above twenty אמות. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second limit on the argument, this time based on the סוכה's size, and asks which reason it matches. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the deciding factor is not the walls but how wide the סוכה is. A wide enough סוכה would be kosher even when very tall. The גמרא wants to know which reason makes width matter.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which
Rav Huna said that Rav said:
The dispute is where it has only
four cubits by four cubits,
but if it has more
than four cubits by four cubits,
even above twenty cubits it is kosher.
In accordance with whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question to step 5, about a different limit on the same argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason for the twenty-אמה limit explains why a wide סוכה is kosher even when very tall?

steps.title: It fits רבי זירא: a wide סוכה gets shade from its roof
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's report follows רבי זירא, who said the limit is about shade. In a wide סוכה, the shade comes from the סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי זירא, who said the reason is shade. Since the סוכה is wide, there is shade from the סוכה's roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this rule matches רבי זירא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said a סוכה must give shade from its סכך. In a narrow, very tall סוכה, the shade comes from the walls, not the roof. In a wide סוכה, the roof itself gives shade, so it is kosher even above twenty אמות.

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Zeira, who says:
It is because of shade,
phrases.notes: In a small, tall סוכה, the shade comes from the walls and not from the roof.

phrases.english: and since it is spacious,
there is shade of the סוכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא, דְּאָמַר: מִשּׁוּם צֵל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7, using רבי זירא's shade reason from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's rule follows רבי זירא, since a wide סוכה gets shade from its סכך.
steps.whatToRemember: Each version of רב follows a different reason. Walls reaching the roof fit רבה (the eye sees it). A סוכה wider than four by four אמות fits רבי זירא (there is shade from the roof).
steps.confusionAlert: Both statements are said in רב's name, but they are reported by two different people and follow two different reasons. Do not mix them together.

steps.title: A third version of רב's rule: the smallest possible סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב חנן בר רבה's report of רב's rule. The tall-סוכה argument applies only to a סוכה that barely fits head, most of body, and table. The גמרא asks which reason this fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רב חנן בר רבה said in the name of רב: the argument is only about a סוכה that holds just enough for a person's head, most of his body, and his table. But if it holds more than that, it is kosher even above twenty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like with the two earlier reports, the גמרא quotes a version of רב's rule. It asks which of the three reasons for the 20-אמה limit it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the size that makes a tall סוכה kosher is very small: anything bigger than the absolute minimum. רב הונא's version (step 7) needed four by four אמות. So the גמרא wants to know which reason could explain this new, much lower line.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument (here, the argument in the משנה about a סוכה taller than 20 אמות)
His head, most of his body, and his table: the smallest size a סוכה can be

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that רב חנן בר רבה said in the name of רב:
The argument is when it does not hold
more than enough for his head, most of his body, and his table,
phrases.notes: In plain English: the סוכה is only just big enough for this, the smallest kosher size.

phrases.english: but if it holds more
than enough for his head, most of his body, and his table,
even above twenty אמות it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third in a series of reports of רב's rule. Each one is matched to one of the reasons for the 20-אמה limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason (רבה's, רבי זירא's, or רבא's) explains the rule that any סוכה bigger than the minimum is kosher even above 20 אמות?

steps.title: It fits none of the reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חנן בר רבה's version matches none of the reasons given.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? It is not like any one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: this version of רב's rule does not fit any of the three reasons for the 20-אמה limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of the three reasons would let a tall סוכה become kosher just because it is a bit bigger than the minimum. Unlike steps 6 and 8, where a match was found, here the גמרא admits that this report stands on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Not like any one (of the opinions)

steps.whatToRemember: Three versions of רב's rule: רבי יאשיה's (walls reach the סכך) fits רבה. רב הונא's (four by four אמות) fits רבי זירא. רב חנן בר רבה's (more than the minimum size) fits none of them.

phrases.english: Like whom? Not like any one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חנן בר רבה's version does not follow any of the three reasons.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה's version clearly differs from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יאשיה's report is clearly different from the other two, because it gives no floor-size measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי יאשיה's version disagrees with רב הונא's and רב חנן בר רבה's, because they give a measurement for the floor size, and he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the three reports of רב's rule. It starts by saying the obvious difference: רבי יאשיה's version is about walls, not about size. This sets up the question about the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה's version depends on whether the walls reach the סכך. The other two depend on how big the floor of the סוכה is. So they clearly disagree. The real puzzle is how רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבה differ, since both talk about size.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (usually followed by 'אֶלָּא', 'but', which brings the real difficulty)
The stretch: the floor area of the סוכה

phrases.english: Granted, רבי יאשיה's statement
phrases.notes: This is the report from step 5, about the walls reaching the סכך.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב חָנָן בַּר רַבָּה,
phrases.english: disagrees with רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבה,
since they give a measurement for the floor size,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיהוּ לָא קָא יָהֵיב שִׁעוּרָא בִּמְשָׁכָא.
phrases.english: and he does not give a measurement for the floor size.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה פְּלִיגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After matching each report to a reason, the גמרא now compares the reports with each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יאשיה's version is about walls, while the other two are about floor size, so the difference is clear.

steps.title: Do רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבה argue about the minimum size of a סוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the two size-based reports differ because they disagree about the smallest kosher סוכה: four by four אמות, or head-most-body-and-table.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבה: shall we say they argue about the minimum size for a kosher סוכה? One holds a kosher סוכה is four אמות, and the other holds it is one that holds his head, most of his body, and his table.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the two size-based reports differ. It suggests that they argue about the smallest size a kosher סוכה can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that each one means 'the argument is only about a minimum-size סוכה'. They just disagree about what that minimum is. רב הונא would hold the minimum is four by four אמות, and רב חנן בר רבה would hold it is head, most of body, and table.

keyTerms.meaning: What makes a סוכה kosher; here, its minimum size
Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא often goes on to reject)
One master holds... and the other master holds

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חָנָן בַּר רַבָּה,
phrases.english: But רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבה,
shall we say they argue about the minimum size of a kosher סוכה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר הֶכְשֵׁר סוּכָּה בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: that one master holds a kosher סוכה is four אמות,
phrases.notes: He means four by four אמות. This is רב הונא.

phrases.english: and the other master holds a kosher סוכה
is one that holds his head, most of his body, and his table?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חָנָן בַּר רַבָּה נֵימָא בְּהֶכְשֵׁר סוּכָּה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the 'בשלמא' of step 11 with the 'אלא': the harder comparison between the two size-based reports.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the difference between רב הונא and רב חנן בר רבה really an argument about the minimum size of a kosher סוכה?

steps.title: No, both agree on the minimum size; they argue about something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both agree the minimum is head, most of body, and table. רב חנן בר רבה holds that the tall-סוכה argument is only about that minimum size, and anything bigger is kosher according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that a kosher סוכה is one that holds his head, most of his body, and his table. Here is what they argue about: one master holds that the argument is about a סוכה that holds just his head, most of his body, and his table. But if it holds more than that, everyone agrees it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 12. Both sages agree on the minimum size. Their real difference is how big a tall סוכה must be to escape the argument. This step lays out רב חנן בר רבה's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum kosher size is not in question: everyone says head, most of body, and table. The question is where the 'tall סוכה' argument stops. According to רב חנן בר רבה, it stops as soon as the סוכה is any bigger than that minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone (here: both sides of the argument in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up two different sizes. The minimum size of any kosher סוכה (head, most of body, table) is agreed by all. What they argue about is how big a tall סוכה must be so that even the stricter opinion would call it kosher.

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees
that a kosher סוכה is one that holds his head, most of his body, and his table.
And here, this is what they argue about:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר בְּמַחְזֶקֶת רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: One master holds that they argue about a סוכה that holds just his head, most of his body, and his table,
phrases.notes: This is רב חנן בר רבה. 'They' are the two sides in the משנה's argument about a tall סוכה.

phrases.english: but if it holds more than his head, most of his body, and his table,
everyone agrees it is kosher,

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הֶכְשֵׁר סוּכָּה רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ וְשׁוּלְחָנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 12 and offers a different way to explain the difference between the two reports.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that they disagree about the minimum size of a kosher סוכה. It keeps the fact that they disagree.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no need to make them argue about the basic minimum size. Both can agree on it and still disagree about where the tall-סוכה argument ends.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps one agreed minimum size for every סוכה. The two reports differ only on how far the argument in the משנה reaches.

steps.title: The other report: the debate covers sizes up to four by four אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its rejection. The second reporter (רב הונא) holds that the tall-סוכה debate covers every size from the minimum up to four by four אמות. Anything bigger is kosher according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage holds that they argue about a סוכה anywhere from the minimum size (head, most of the body, and table) up to four by four אמות. But if it is bigger than four by four אמות, everyone agrees it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it started in Step 13 by explaining the second reporter's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reporters agree on the smallest kosher סוכה. They differ only on how far the tall-סוכה argument reaches. For רב חנן בר רבה it covers only the minimum size. For the other Sage it reaches up to four by four אמות.
steps.whatToRemember: The two size-based reports do not argue about the minimum סוכה. They only argue about how wide a סוכה must be before a very tall one becomes kosher: just above the minimum, or above four by four אמות.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds
phrases.notes: "The other Sage" is the second reporter of רב's rule, the one who mentioned four by four אמות.

phrases.english: that from one that holds his head, most of his body, and his table
up to four cubits, they disagree;
but if it is more than four cubits,
everyone agrees it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 13 by giving the second reporter's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion in Step 12 that the two reports argue about the minimum סוכה size.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reports really differ only on how far the tall-סוכה debate reaches, not on the minimum size.

steps.title: An objection: a ברייתא where רבי יהודה allows a very tall סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב. The חכמים say a סוכה taller than twenty אמות is not kosher, and רבי יהודה allows it up to forty or fifty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: a סוכה that is taller than twenty אמות is not kosher. רבי יהודה says it is kosher, even up to forty or fifty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an objection against רב by quoting a ברייתא. It is setting up the challenge, which will be explained in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes on to tell a story about a queen's tall סוכה. The גמרא will use that story to test the different reports of רב's rule. Before pressing the objection, the גמרא first reads through the whole ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty אמות, the height limit of a סוכה
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A sukka that is high
above twenty cubits
is not kosher;
and Rabbi Yehuda declares it kosher
up to forty or fifty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how the reports of רב differ, the גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reports of רב's rule limiting the argument over a סוכה taller than twenty אמות (steps 5, 7, 9)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the height debate is quoted to test רב. The exact attack has not been spelled out yet.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's proof from הילני המלכה's tall סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה proves his view from a story. הילני המלכה had a סוכה taller than twenty אמות, and the זקנים went in and out of it without telling her anything was wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: there was a story with הילני המלכה in לוד. Her סוכה was taller than twenty אמות. The זקנים went in and out of it, and they did not say a word to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה backs up his view with a real event. The זקנים saw a very tall סוכה and did not object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the זקנים staying silent. If a סוכה taller than twenty אמות were not kosher, they would have said so. Since they said nothing, it must be kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an actual event used as a proof
Lod, a city in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with Queen Helene in Lod
whose sukka was higher than twenty cubits,
and the Elders were going in and out there,
and they did not say a word to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּהֵילֶנִי הַמַּלְכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבי יהודה's proof for his view.
steps.raayaObject: A סוכה taller than twenty אמות is kosher.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The זקנים said nothing about הילני המלכה's tall סוכה.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: she was a woman
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that this story proves nothing. הילני was a woman, and women do not have to sit in a סוכה, so the זקנים had no reason to comment.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? She was a woman, and women do not have to sit in a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים knock down רבי יהודה's proof by giving another reason the זקנים stayed quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence only proves something if the סוכה had to be kosher. A woman does not have to sit in a סוכה at all. So the זקנים may have said nothing even if her סוכה was not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? Used to reject a proof
Not required to sit in a סוכה

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים who say a סוכה over twenty אמות is not kosher.

phrases.english: Is that a proof?
She was a woman
and exempt from the מצוה of sukka.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the זקנים' silence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A woman does not have to sit in a סוכה, so there was no need to comment on her סוכה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה answers: her seven sons, and she followed the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה defends his proof with two points. She had seven sons who needed a kosher סוכה, and she did everything only the way the חכמים told her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: But she had seven sons! And besides, everything she did, she did only according to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה rescues his proof with two separate answers to the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: even if she did not need a kosher סוכה, her sons did, so the זקנים should have spoken up. Second answer: she followed the חכמים in everything, so her סוכה must have been built the way they said was correct.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…, used to push back
And furthermore, adds a second argument

phrases.english: He said to them:
But didn't she have seven sons?
And furthermore: all her actions

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עָשְׂתָה אֶלָּא עַל פִּי חֲכָמִים.
phrases.english: she did only according to the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: וַהֲלֹא שִׁבְעָה בָּנִים הֲווֹ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' rejection in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings new facts that bring back the force of the proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because she was a woman, the זקנים had no reason to comment on her סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her sons needed a kosher סוכה, and she followed the חכמים in everything, so the זקנים' silence does prove the סוכה was kosher.

steps.title: Why did רבי יהודה need his second argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה added "and furthermore, she did everything according to the חכמים." The point about her seven sons already seems to be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he need to add: "And furthermore, everything she did, she did only according to the חכמים"?
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא against רב, the גמרא stops to ask why רבי יהודה gave a second argument. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her seven sons needed a kosher סוכה, the proof already stands. The extra argument looks unneeded. The גמרא expects there must be a reason the first argument alone was not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? Asks why something extra was said

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet the objection against רב. The גמרא is first making sure it understands the ברייתא. The challenge to רב comes later.

phrases.english: Why do I need it to teach:
"And furthermore, all her actions

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עָשְׂתָה אֶלָּא עַל פִּי חֲכָמִים״?
phrases.english: she did only according to the Sages"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why רבי יהודה needed the second argument in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the second argument (she followed the חכמים) was needed, when the seven sons seem to be enough.

steps.title: At least one of seven sons was old enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's first point answers the claim that her sons were minors and therefore exempt. Among seven sons, at least one must have been old enough not to need his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יהודה meant: if you say her sons were young, and young children don't have to sit in a סוכה, then answer this. She had seven sons, so at least one of them must have been old enough not to need his mother all the time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question from step 19 by explaining what the 'seven sons' point was meant to prove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים could argue that the sons were small children, who are exempt from סוכה, so the זקנים had no reason to comment. רבי יהודה replies that with seven sons, at least one had to be old enough not to need his mother. A child at that age must sit in a סוכה as part of his training, so the זקנים should have objected if the סוכה was not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. The גמרא is explaining someone's words more fully.
A minor, a child who is not yet bar מצוה
Exempt, not required to do the מצוה
A child who no longer needs his mother constantly. At this age he must start training in the מצוה of סוכה.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהודה, speaking to the חכמים.

phrases.english: If you say they were minor sons,
and minors are exempt from the sukkah,
since they were seven,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא הָוֵי בְּהוּ חַד
phrases.english: it is impossible that there was not one among them
who no longer needed his mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 19's question about why רבי יהודה added 'and furthermore.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה needed the extra point after mentioning the seven sons
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven-sons point answers the claim that all the sons were minors: at least one was old enough not to need his mother, so he was obligated in סוכה. The reason the second point is needed comes in the next step.

steps.title: She kept even rabbinic rules
steps.stepSummary: A child's obligation at that age is only מדרבנן. That is why רבי יהודה added that she did everything according to the חכמים, which shows she kept rabbinic rules too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that a child who doesn't need his mother is obligated only by rabbinic law, and the queen didn't care about rabbinic laws, then listen to what רבי יהודה added: 'and furthermore, she did all her actions only according to the חכמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer: the 'and furthermore' point blocks a second objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if one son was old enough, his obligation to sit in a סוכה is only מדרבנן. Someone could say הילני kept only Torah laws, so the זקנים saw no need to tell her anything. The added point, that she followed the חכמים in everything, shows she kept rabbinic rules too. So both of רבי יהודה's points are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not a direct Torah obligation
She did not pay attention to it, did not keep it
According to the instructions of the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: Each of רבי יהודה's two points answers a different objection. The seven sons prove that one child was old enough for חינוך. Following the חכמים in everything proves she kept that rabbinic obligation.

phrases.english: And if you say
a child who no longer needs his mother
is obligated only by rabbinic law,
and she did not pay attention to rabbinic law,
come and hear:
and furthermore, all her actions she did not do
except according to the Sages.
phrases.notes: This is the same line רבי יהודה said back in step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימְרוּ קָטָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְאִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 20 by explaining the second point.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the 'and furthermore' clause is needed
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It shows that הילני kept rabbinic obligations, including her older son's rabbinic duty to sit in a סוכה.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits the view about walls not reaching the roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts testing the ברייתא against the different ways of explaining רב's ruling. It first notes that the ברייתא fits nicely with the view that the מחלוקת is about walls that do not reach the סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to the one who said the מחלוקת is about a סוכה whose walls do not reach the roof, because it is normal for a queen to sit in a סוכה whose walls do not reach the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It first shows which explanation of רב fits the הילני story easily, and the difficulty with the other views will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, different אמוראים explained what case רב's ruling is about. According to the view that the argument is only about a סוכה whose walls stop short of the סכך, the הילני story makes sense. A queen's סוכה would normally be built that way. The word בשלמא signals that another view will have trouble explaining the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works well for this view. It signals that a difficulty for another view is coming.
A dispute, here between רבי יהודה and the חכמים
The roof covering of the סוכה
The normal way of a queen

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only the first half of the challenge. The בשלמא part says what works well, and the problem for another view comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said
phrases.notes: This is רבי יאשיה, who quoted רב earlier on this דף.

phrases.english: the dispute is where the walls do not reach the roofing,
it is the way of a queen to sit
in a sukkah whose walls do not reach the roofing,

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי יהודה's proof to checking how the ברייתא fits each explanation of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The other explanations of רב's ruling (the target comes after this line)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הילני story fits naturally with a סוכה whose walls do not reach the סכך. That raises the question of how the story fits the views that explain the מחלוקת differently.
